tdit214.title: TDIT 214 — Object-Oriented Programming with Java I
tdit214.description: Introduces learners to Java as an OOP language covering data structures, algorithms and practical application development.
tdit214.outline: This module imparts knowledge of programming data structures and algorithms. It introduces the learner to object-oriented programming language Java. By the end learners should acquire advanced practical skills in OOP as well as design and development of computer application programs using Java.

modules.title: Introduction to Java

slides.title: Welcome to Java
bullets: Java is a high-level, class-based, object-oriented programming language
Write Once, Run Anywhere — compiles to bytecode for any JVM
Powers Android apps, web backends, and enterprise systems
Created by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems in 1995

slides.title: Core Concepts
bullets: Class — a blueprint defining properties and behaviours
Object — a live instance created from a class
Inheritance — a child class inherits from a parent
Interface — a contract defining what a class must implement

slides.title: Your Development Environment
bullets: JDK — Java Development Kit, includes the compiler
JRE — Java Runtime Environment, runs compiled programs
IDE options: IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, VS Code
javac compiles .java files; java command runs them

modules.codeNote: The class name must match the filename. main() is where the JVM starts. System.out.println() prints a line to the console. We declare a String and an int then concatenate them with the + operator.

modules.title: Object-Oriented Features

slides.title: Primitive Data Types
bullets: int — whole numbers: int age = 20;
double — decimals: double gpa = 4.10;
boolean — true or false: boolean passed = true;
char — single character: char grade = 'A';
String — text (not primitive but commonly used)

slides.title: Arrays
bullets: Arrays hold multiple values of the same type
Declaration: int[] marks = new int[5];
Initialiser: int[] marks = {78, 85, 92};
Index is zero-based — first element is marks[0]
.length gives the number of elements

slides.title: Operators
bullets: Arithmetic: + − * / % (modulo)
Assignment: = += -= *= /=
Comparison: == != > < >= <= (return boolean)
Logical: && (AND)  || (OR)  ! (NOT)
Ternary: result = (a > b) ? a : b;

modules.codeNote: Five primitive variables are declared. The marks array uses an initialiser — the size is inferred automatically. marks.length returns 5. The last three lines demonstrate arithmetic, modulo and comparison operators.

modules.title: Classes & Objects

slides.title: Anatomy of a Class
bullets: Fields — data the object holds
Constructor — initialises the object when created
Methods — actions the object can perform
Access modifiers: public, private, protected
this keyword refers to the current object

slides.title: Constructors
bullets: Same name as the class, no return type
Called when you write: new ClassName()
You can overload constructors with different parameters
super() calls the parent class constructor

slides.title: Encapsulation
bullets: Make fields private
Provide public getters and setters
Setters can validate data before storing
Hides internal details from outside code

modules.codeNote: Fields are private so outside code cannot access them directly. The constructor uses this.name to distinguish the field from the parameter. The setter validates the GPA before storing it. Two Student objects are created from the same class blueprint.

modules.title: Control Flow & Conditionals

slides.title: if / else if / else
bullets: Executes a block only when its condition is true
Conditions are boolean expressions: a > b, x == 5
else if chains allow multiple paths
else is the catch-all fallback

slides.title: Loops
bullets: for — best when iteration count is known
while — repeats while condition is true
do-while — always executes at least once
for-each — iterate arrays: for(int m : marks)
break exits; continue skips to next iteration

slides.title: switch Statement
bullets: Matches a value against fixed cases
Each case must end with break
default handles unmatched values
Cleaner than long if-else if chains

modules.codeNote: The if-else chain maps score to grade. The for loop accumulates marks and divides for the average. The for-each loop prints all marks on one line. The switch maps a char grade to feedback — every case ends with break to prevent fall-through.

modules.title: Interfaces & Inheritance

slides.title: Inheritance
bullets: class Dog extends Animal — Dog is child, Animal is parent
Child inherits all non-private fields and methods
super() calls the parent constructor
A class can only extend ONE parent

slides.title: Polymorphism & Overriding
bullets: @Override — child redefines a parent method
At runtime Java calls the actual object's version
Animal a = new Dog() — reference Animal, object Dog
a.speak() calls Dog's speak() — that is polymorphism

slides.title: Interfaces
bullets: Declared with the interface keyword
All methods are abstract by default
A class implements an interface: implements Speakable
One class can implement multiple interfaces

modules.codeNote: Speakable is an interface with an abstract method and a default method. Dog and Cat both extend Animal and implement Speakable. The zoo array holds Animal references but actual objects are Dog and Cat — calling speak() invokes the correct overridden version. That is runtime polymorphism.

modules.title: Graphics & Databases

slides.title: Java Swing Basics
bullets: JFrame — the top-level window
JPanel — a container to organise components
JLabel — displays text or an image
JButton — a clickable button
JTextField — single-line text input

slides.title: Event Handling
bullets: ActionListener handles button clicks
addActionListener(e -> { ... }) — lambda syntax
MouseListener for mouse events
SwingUtilities.invokeLater() — always build GUI on EDT

slides.title: JDBC — Database Connectivity
bullets: JDBC = Java Database Connectivity
Connect: DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, pass)
Execute: Statement.executeQuery() returns ResultSet
Iterate ResultSet row by row
Always close connection when done

modules.codeNote: We extend JFrame and add components with FlowLayout. The lambda inside addActionListener runs when Submit is clicked. It reads both fields, parses GPA as a double, and shows a Dean's List message for GPA 4.0 and above. SwingUtilities.invokeLater keeps everything on the Event Dispatch Thread.
